sentences.text: The petitioner has been conducting a smoke emission testing centre for diesel and petrol engine vehicles pursuant to the licence issued through Ext.P1.

The petitioner complains that the 10th and 11th respondents blocked the user ID of the petitioner's testing station on 07.03.2024 without any reason and without issuing any notice to him, in spite of the validity of Ext.P1 till 28.04.2024.
The petitioner also challenges Clause No.1 in Ext.P2, which is a communication dated 16.04.2023 issued by the Transport Commissioner.

2. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the 6 th respondent stating that an inspection was carried out at the petitioner's pollution testing centre on 07.03.2024, in which it was revealed that the person testing the vehicle was not a licensed 2025:KER:83989 operator.
It is mandatory to exhibit the licence of the firm, the operator's qualification and the training certificates as per the relevant orders.
It is stated that one Thirunavukkarasu was the licenced operator, but one Arun, who was testing the vehicles, was not qualified.
It was under such circumstances that the ID was blocked.

The petitioner was directed to produce the documents with an application to change the operator if he wishes to employ another person, and an assurance was also given that the centre ID would be unblocked soon after a new operator is engaged.
3. Learned Government Pleader, on instructions, that a consolidated circular has already been issued on 07.05.2025 as regards the pollution testing centres.
4. Upon admission of the writ petition, an interim order was passed on 19th April, 2024, directing the unblocking of the ID.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the interim order was complied with and the licence was renewed.

6. As regards the second prayer challenging Ext.P2 circular as stated above, in view of the introduction of Circular No.9 of 2025 2025:KER:83989 dated 07.05.2025 issued by the Transport Commissioner, the second prayer sought in the writ petition does not survive for consideration.
The petitioner has also prayed for compensation for the loss sustained during the period when the user ID remained blocked.
It will be open to the petitioner to approach a competent civil court claiming that relief, as it requires a factual adjudication.
